A crew of 4 movers with a truck runs $200–$300 an hour on the calculator's planning rates, and a 3-bedroom home moved 10 road miles costs $1,150–$2,850 off peak, with no stairs and no extras. That is the starting point for how much do movers cost in Philadelphia, where the usual home is a rowhouse with narrow stairs, no driveway and a truck that has to find space on the street.

Bedrooms are the quickest guide, because they set the crew size and the hours. The table gives the rate table's range for a local move of 10 road miles, off peak, and what having the crew pack would add. These are national planning figures, not Philadelphia quotes, and the city's stairs and parking tend to push a job up the range.

A local crew bills by the hour: $50–$75 for each mover, truck included, so 2 movers for a small apartment cost $100–$150 an hour and 5 movers for a large house cost $250–$375 an hour. When you ask how much do movers cost in Philadelphia, the hours a house takes matter more than the miles between the two addresses.

Rowhouses, trinities and twins: why the stairs matter

Most of Philadelphia's homes are attached houses, and their stairs shape the bill. A typical rowhouse has a narrow, steep staircase, and a trinity, the city's three-story house with one room per floor, often has a winding stair that a sofa or a box spring can't turn. Pieces that won't fit may have to come apart, or in some cases leave through a window, which takes extra crew and equipment priced on its own.

Many older homes add a basement flight as well. Measure the tightest turn on each staircase and the doors at both ends before the estimate, and tell the mover about every flight. Stairs are the biggest reason how much do movers cost in Philadelphia varies between two homes with the same number of bedrooms, and the calculator's stairs option raises the range to match.

Getting a truck close on a Philadelphia street

Few rowhouse blocks have driveways, and many streets are narrow and one-way, so where the truck stands decides how far the crew carries each piece. A truck at your door keeps the job short. A truck around the corner adds a long carry to every trip, billed as time or as a separate fee.

The city's answer is a Temporary No Parking permit from the Department of Streets, which reserves curb space for the truck and needs signs posted before the day. The lead times and sign rules are in the city rules below. Ask whether your mover applies for the permit or leaves it to you, and whether its cost is in the quote, since a reserved space can lower how much do movers cost in Philadelphia by cutting the carry.

When Philadelphia movers are busiest

The calculator prices May to September as peak season, and a summer date raises both ends of the range. Philadelphia adds its own rush around the universities: neighborhoods near Penn, Drexel and Temple fill with student moves at the end of the spring term and in late August, before the fall term. Leases that end on the last day of the month crowd the last few days of each month too.

A weekday in the middle of the month, outside summer, is the easiest date to book and gives the lowest answer to how much do movers cost in Philadelphia on the calculator. Weekends and month-ends fill first, so if your lease forces one of those dates, book early.

Labor only and other ways to spend less

If you rent the truck yourself, you can still hire hands for the heavy lifting. A labor-only crew of 2 movers costs $80–$130 an hour without a truck, or $200–$520 to load, $200–$460 to unload and $320–$910 for both ends, off peak with no extras. That route suits a short move across the city, where you drive the truck and the crew handles the stairs.

  • Move less. Every piece you sell or donate is a trip the crew doesn't make up and down a narrow staircase.
  • Pack before the crew arrives. Boxes taped and labeled let paid hours go on carrying, and the box estimator below counts what you need.
  • Take beds and tables apart yourself. On a winding trinity stair, furniture that comes apart in advance saves the crew that time.

Each of these trims the hours, and the hours are most of how much do movers cost in Philadelphia on a local move.

A worked example: a 3-bedroom rowhouse to the Northeast

Take a 3-bedroom rowhouse in South Philadelphia moving about 10 road miles to a twin in Northeast Philadelphia on a weekday in October. Here is how much do movers cost in Philadelphia for that house, line by line:

  • Movers: 4 movers at $200–$300 an hour, and $1,150–$2,850 for the move on the calculator's terms with no stairs. Two full flights at the old house and one at the new one push it up the range.
  • Packing: $800–$1,800 if the crew packs, or, if you pack, $1.82–$2.69 for each medium box and $2.26–$3.42 for each large one, typical published prices.
  • Permit: a Temporary No Parking permit for the truck's space at the old house, applied for ahead of time.
  • Tips: $20.00–$65.00 per mover for a full working day is a typical published figure.

The same house moved in July falls in peak season, and a longer drive to the suburbs adds time on the road. The calculator above prices your own date, stairs and distance, and shows how much do movers cost in Philadelphia for your house.

How much do movers cost in Philadelphia for an out-of-state move

The Delaware River is a state line. A move from Philadelphia to Camden, Cherry Hill or anywhere else in New Jersey is interstate, however short, so FMCSA requires the mover to have a USDOT number. A move that stays in Pennsylvania falls to the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission, which regulates household goods movers in the state.

For longer moves the price works differently: weight and road miles replace hours. A 3-bedroom home moved 1,000 road miles costs $4,000–$8,550 on the calculator's planning terms, off peak with no stairs or extras, about $4.04–$8.50 per mile spread across the trip. The distance table below prices a move from the city to ten major metros, from New York to Atlanta, and shows how much do movers cost in Philadelphia once the hours stop being the main cost.

Spotting a fair Philadelphia quote

Get at least three written estimates, each after a walk-through in person or on video, and give every mover the same list of rooms, stairs and dates. Then watch for FMCSA's warning signs: a price quoted without anyone seeing your home, cash or a big deposit demanded up front, or blank forms put in front of you to sign. FMCSA's red flags are worth checking for any mover, local or long distance.

Set each estimate against the range the calculator above gives for your home, stairs and date. A quote far below it usually leaves out stairs, a long carry or hours that come back on moving day. That comparison is the surest way to know how much do movers cost in Philadelphia for your home before you sign.

Philadelphia permit and sign rules for moving trucks

Holding curb space is part of how much do movers cost in Philadelphia, because a truck parked down the block means a longer carry. These Department of Streets rules cover permits, signs and containers, each with its source.

Apply for a Temporary No Parking permit 4 business days ahead

The Department of Streets issues Temporary No Parking permits for moving trucks. Apply at least four business days before you need the permit, with the truck's length and the permit's start and end time.

Source: City of Philadelphia Department of Streets, checked 28 October 2026

Post the no-parking signs at least 24 hours ahead

Take the printed permit to a Philadelphia police district headquarters, which gives you the temporary no parking signs. Post them as soon as you receive the permit, or at least 24 hours before you need the spaces.

Source: City of Philadelphia Department of Streets, checked 28 October 2026

Keep a moving container or pod on the street up to five days

The Department of Streets' Temporary No Parking permits also cover storage containers or pods. A moving container or pod can stay parked for a maximum of five days.

Source: City of Philadelphia Department of Streets, checked 28 October 2026

Tipping a Philadelphia crew after the stairs

Tips sit outside how much do movers cost in Philadelphia on the bill. Work out what tipping guides suggest for each mover, by the hour, by the day or as a share, for the crew you book.

3 movers 4–6.5 hours

Per mover $16–$98

For the crew $48–$294

Who to tip and when

  • Tipping is up to you: guides call a tip a thank-you for good work, not an obligation. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides find cash simplest, handed to each mover at the end of the job. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, This Old House, MoveAdvisor and CNET)
  • When one crew loads and another unloads, guides suggest tipping each crew after it finishes its part. (HireAHelper, CNET, Real Simple, American Van Lines and NerdWallet)
  • On a move of several days, guides suggest tipping at the end of each day, in case the crew changes. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet and Forbes Home)
  • Guides suggest a separate tip for a separate packing crew. (CNET and This Old House)
  • Guides suggest asking the moving company about its tipping policy first: some build gratuity into the price, and some don't accept tips. (Forbes Home, This Old House and U-Haul)
  • Guides suggest tipping more for stairs, heavy furniture or bad weather, and less, or nothing, for damage, a late start or careless work. (HireAHelper, NerdWallet, CNET and Real Simple)
  • Drinks and snacks are welcome, but guides don't count them as the tip. (NerdWallet and CNET)

Philadelphia move checklist, from estimates to keys

Getting three estimates early protects how much do movers cost in Philadelphia from last-minute rates. Enter your moving date and each task, from listing what moves to reporting damage, shows up on its due date.

0 of 14 done

8 weeks before

  • Give every company the same list, so their estimates price the same job.

  • A second date gives you room if the company you want is booked.

  • Give each one the same details, so the prices compare like for like.

6 weeks before

  • Know what it costs to change the date or cancel, and how much notice you must give.

4 weeks before

  • Get close-ups of any damage that's already there, so a claim later is clear.

  • Have the old place stop the day after you leave, and the new place start the day before you arrive.

2 weeks before

  • Keep the backup apart from the devices on moving day.

  • Plan how those will travel, or give them away before moving day.

1 week before

  • Chargers, basic tools, toilet paper, cleaning supplies, snacks and a change of clothes.

The day before

  • Eat down the frozen food in the weeks before, so little is left to throw away.

  • Tape a sign on it, or gather it in one room, so it isn't loaded by mistake.

  • So nothing holds up the end of the job.

Moving day

Questions

How much do movers cost in Philadelphia? FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

How much do movers cost in Philadelphia per hour?

On the calculator's planning rates, a local crew with a truck costs $100–$150 an hour for 2 movers and $250–$375 an hour for 5, which is $50–$75 for each mover. A 3-bedroom rowhouse usually takes 4. Those hourly figures are the core of how much do movers cost in Philadelphia, and stairs or a long carry add hours to them.

How much should each mover get as a tip?

Tipping is your choice. Published guides suggest $20.00–$65.00 for each mover for a full working day, less for a half day, or a share of the total bill. Tip at the high end after a day of narrow rowhouse stairs, and let the tip calculator on this page total it for your crew.

What hidden costs can show up on a Philadelphia moving bill?

The usual extras are stairs, a long carry from a truck that couldn't park close, minimum hours, travel time from the depot, packing materials and any parking permit. Ask each mover to name every fee on the written estimate, so how much do movers cost in Philadelphia on the day matches the quote.

What does a 1,000-square-foot rowhouse cost to move?

A home of about 1,000 square feet usually has 2 bedrooms, so start from $720–$1,800 for a local move of 10 road miles, off peak with no stairs or extras. A rowhouse that size often has two narrow flights, which pushes it up the range. Enter your bedrooms and stairs in the calculator for your own figure.

How can you tell if a Philadelphia mover is legitimate?

For a move within Pennsylvania, check that the company holds authority from the Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission. For a move to New Jersey or farther, look up its USDOT number with FMCSA. Be wary of an estimate given sight unseen, a demand for a large cash deposit, or blank papers to sign.
